---
title: "Other content elements"
order: 4
---

Use code blocks, block quotes, horizontal rules, and collapsible content to structure content and make it easier for participants to engage. 

Each example below shows the Markdown syntax and how it appears when rendered.

<br>

## Code blocks

Use code blocks to display code or other text that should keep its formatting. Add the language after the opening backticks to enable syntax highlighting where supported.

**Markdown syntax**

````markdown
```python
print("Hello, participants!")
````


**Rendered result**

```python
print("Hello, participants!")
```

## Block quotes

Use a block quote to set apart a quotation or a statement from another source.

**Markdown syntax**

```markdown
> Clear structure helps readers navigate information and focus on the main message.
```

**Rendered result**

> Clear structure helps readers navigate information and focus on the main message.

## Horizontal rules

A horizontal rule can separate distinct parts of a page. Use it sparingly, when a visual break helps clarify the structure.

**Markdown syntax**

```markdown
---
```

**Rendered result**

Before the horizontal rule.

---

After the horizontal rule.


## Collapsible content

Use a collapsible section to place supplementary information that readers can expand when they want to see more. This is useful for optional details, explanations, or answers to questions.

**Markdown syntax**

```html
<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

This content is hidden until the reader expands the section.

</details>
```

**Rendered result**

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

This content is hidden until the reader expands the section.

</details>

::: {.callout-note}
The `<details>` example uses HTML rather than Markdown, which is appropriate here: it demonstrates a Quarto-supported way to create expandable content without using a callout box.
:::
